title: 满庭芳·夏日溧水无想山作
title_en: Man Ting Fang: Written on Wuxiang Mountain at Lishui in Summer
author: 周邦彦

form.zh: 词，词牌《满庭芳》，双调九十五字
form.en: ci to the tune Man Ting Fang, 95 characters in two stanzas

text_note.zh: 这里用通行本。语料库本“炉烟”作“垆烟”，是不同版本的写法。
text_note.en: This page uses the common text. The corpus writes lú (burner) with a different character, as some old editions do.

readings.zh: “溅溅”在这里读 jiān jiān，形容流水的声音，不读 jiàn。
readings.en: Here the doubled character is read jiān jiān, the sound of flowing water, not jiàn (to splash).

readings.zh: “长近”的“长”读 cháng，意思是常常、长久。
readings.en: In cháng jìn this character is read cháng, meaning always or often.

glosses.zh: 风老莺雏：暖风吹着，小黄莺长大了。老，这里是使……长大的意思。雏，刚出生不久的小鸟。
glosses.en: fēng lǎo yīng chú: the warm wind has made the young orioles grow up. Chú is a baby bird.

glosses.zh: 雨肥梅子：雨水让梅子长得又大又圆。
glosses.en: yǔ féi méi zǐ: the rain has made the plums plump.

glosses.zh: 午阴嘉树清圆：中午时，好看的大树投下清清楚楚、圆圆的树荫。嘉树，美好的树。
glosses.en: wǔ yīn jiā shù qīng yuán: at noon the fine trees cast clear, round shade. Jiā shù means a lovely tree.

glosses.zh: 地卑：地势低洼。
glosses.en: dì bēi: low-lying ground.

glosses.zh: 衣润费炉烟：衣服潮湿，要费不少炉火的烟来熏干。
glosses.en: yī rùn fèi lú yān: clothes are damp, and it takes a lot of smoke from the burner to dry them.

glosses.zh: 乌鸢：乌鸦和老鹰。
glosses.en: wū yuān: crows and kites.

glosses.zh: 新绿：新涨的绿色春水。
glosses.en: xīn lǜ: the fresh green water that has newly risen.

glosses.zh: 溅溅：流水的声音。
glosses.en: jiān jiān: the sound of running water.

glosses.zh: 凭栏：靠着栏杆。
glosses.en: píng lán: leaning on the railing.

glosses.zh: 黄芦苦竹：黄色的芦苇和苦竹。白居易被贬到江州（今江西九江）时，在《琵琶行》里说自己住的地方“黄芦苦竹绕宅生”。
glosses.en: huáng lú kǔ zhú: yellow reeds and bitter bamboo. When Bai Juyi was sent down to Jiangzhou (today's Jiujiang), he wrote in his "Song of the Pipa" that yellow reeds and bitter bamboo grew all round his house.

glosses.zh: 拟泛九江船：打算像白居易那样坐船去九江。意思是自己的处境像被贬的白居易一样。拟，打算。
glosses.en: nǐ fàn jiǔ jiāng chuán: thinking of sailing a boat to Jiujiang like Bai Juyi; his situation feels like that of the exiled poet. Nǐ means to plan to.

glosses.zh: 社燕：燕子春社时飞来，秋社时飞走，所以叫社燕。社，古代春秋两季祭土地神的日子。
glosses.en: shè yàn: swallows that come at the spring festival of the land god and leave at the autumn one. Shè was the day to worship the god of the earth.

glosses.zh: 瀚海：大沙漠，这里指遥远的地方。
glosses.en: hàn hǎi: a vast desert; here, places far away.

glosses.zh: 修椽：长长的屋椽。燕子在屋椽上做窝。修，长。
glosses.en: xiū chuán: long roof rafters, where swallows build their nests. Xiū means long.

glosses.zh: 身外：自身以外的事，比如名利。
glosses.en: shēn wài: things outside oneself, such as fame and money.

glosses.zh: 尊前：酒杯前。尊，同“樽”，酒杯。
glosses.en: zūn qián: in front of the wine cup. Zūn means a wine vessel.

glosses.zh: 倦客：在外面漂泊得疲倦的人，作者自指。
glosses.en: juàn kè: a traveller tired of wandering; the poet means himself.

glosses.zh: 不堪：受不了。
glosses.en: bù kān: cannot bear.

glosses.zh: 急管繁弦：急促的管乐、繁杂的弦乐，指热闹的音乐。
glosses.en: jí guǎn fán xián: fast pipes and busy strings, that is, loud lively music.

glosses.zh: 歌筵畔：唱歌喝酒的宴席旁边。
glosses.en: gē yán pàn: beside the feast with songs.

glosses.zh: 簟枕：竹席和枕头。簟，竹席。
glosses.en: diàn zhěn: a bamboo mat and a pillow. Diàn is a bamboo sleeping mat.

translation.zh: 暖风吹着，小黄莺长大了；
translation.en: The wind has grown the young orioles;

translation.zh: 雨水浇着，梅子长肥了；
translation.en: the rain has fattened the plums;

translation.zh: 中午，美丽的大树投下清晰圆圆的树荫。
translation.en: at noon the fine trees cast clear, round shade.

translation.zh: 这里地势低洼，又靠近山，
translation.en: The ground is low and the hills are near,

translation.zh: 衣服总是潮的，要费很多炉烟去熏干。
translation.en: clothes stay damp and use up much smoke from the burner.

translation.zh: 四周很安静，乌鸦和老鹰自在快乐，
translation.en: All is quiet; crows and kites enjoy themselves;

translation.zh: 小桥外面，新涨的绿水哗哗地流。
translation.en: beyond the little bridge the new green water babbles.

translation.zh: 我靠着栏杆站了很久，
translation.en: I lean on the railing a long while;

translation.zh: 看到黄芦苇和苦竹，
translation.en: seeing yellow reeds and bitter bamboo,

translation.zh: 真想像白居易那样坐船去九江。
translation.en: I feel like taking a boat to Jiujiang, like Bai Juyi.

translation.zh: 一年又一年，
translation.en: Year after year,

translation.zh: 我就像社燕一样，
translation.en: I am like the swallows of the land-god days,

translation.zh: 从遥远的地方飘来飘去，
translation.en: drifting across far-off wastes,

translation.zh: 来到别人的屋椽上暂时寄住。
translation.en: coming to lodge for a while on someone's long rafters.

translation.zh: 还是别去想身外的名利了，
translation.en: Let me not think of things beyond myself,

translation.zh: 常常守在酒杯前吧。
translation.en: but stay close to the wine cup.

translation.zh: 我这个憔悴疲倦的江南游子，
translation.en: I, a worn-out, weary traveller in the south,

translation.zh: 受不了听那急促热闹的音乐。
translation.en: cannot bear to hear the fast pipes and busy strings.

translation.zh: 在歌舞宴席旁边，
translation.en: Beside the singing feast,

translation.zh: 请先替我铺好竹席和枕头，
translation.en: please lay out a bamboo mat and pillow first,

translation.zh: 让我喝醉了就在这里睡一觉。
translation.en: so that when I am drunk I can sleep.

background.zh: 溧水在今天江苏南京南边，无想山是那里的一座山。一般认为这首词作于宋哲宗元祐八年（1093年）前后，那时周邦彦在溧水做县令。他年轻时在京城很受赏识，后来却长年在外地做小官，到处漂泊。这首词写江南初夏的景色，也写他在外做官多年的疲倦。具体年份另有说法。
background.en: Lishui is south of today's Nanjing in Jiangsu, and Wuxiang is a mountain there. The poem is usually dated to around 1093, when Zhou Bangyan was the county magistrate of Lishui. As a young man he was admired in the capital, but later he spent many years in small posts far away, moving from place to place. The poem paints early summer in the south, and also his weariness after years of serving away from home. Some give a different year.

author_note.zh: 周邦彦（1056—1121），字美成，号清真居士，北宋词人。他精通音乐，能自己作曲，作词特别讲究音律和用字，被后人尊为婉约派的大家。他的词常常把前人的诗句化用得不露痕迹，这首词里就借用了白居易和杜甫的诗意。
author_note.en: Zhou Bangyan (1056–1121) was a Northern Song ci poet. He knew music deeply and could compose tunes himself, and he was very careful with rhythm, sound and wording. Later readers honoured him as a master of the gentle, delicate style. He often wove lines from earlier poets into his own so smoothly you can hardly see the seams; this poem borrows ideas from Bai Juyi and Du Fu.

appreciation.zh: 开头三句是一幅初夏小画：小莺长大了，梅子长肥了，中午的树荫又清又圆。一个“老”字、一个“肥”字，把风和雨写得像会养东西一样，非常新鲜。接着写南方的潮湿和安静，乌鸦老鹰都很自在，人却站在栏杆边，看着黄芦苦竹，想起被贬的白居易。下片说自己像社燕一样，年年飘到别人屋檐下暂住。干脆别想那些身外的事，多喝几杯吧。可是热闹的音乐又听不下去，只想先铺好竹席，醉了就睡。看起来很洒脱，其实是很深的倦意和无奈。
appreciation.en: The first three lines are a little picture of early summer: the young orioles have grown, the plums are plump, and the noon shade is clear and round. The words "grown" and "fattened" make the wind and rain seem to raise living things, which feels very fresh. Next come the damp and the quiet of the south. Crows and kites are at ease, but the poet stands at the railing, looks at the yellow reeds and bitter bamboo, and thinks of the exiled Bai Juyi. In the second stanza he says he is like a swallow, lodging under someone else's roof year after year. Better not to think of things beyond himself and simply drink. Yet he cannot bear the loud music either; he only wants a bamboo mat so he can sleep when drunk. It sounds carefree, but underneath is deep tiredness and helplessness.
